summary: This FATF-Egmont Group publication (March 2021) lists trade-based money laundering (TBML) risk indicators drawn from FIU and FATF case data, grouped into structural, trade activity, trade document/commodity, and account/transaction categories. Indicators include complex corporate structures involving shell companies, mass-registration addresses, nominee owners, unreasonably low profit margins consistent with over- or under-invoicing, inconsistent or falsified trade documents, vague commodity descriptions, pay-through/transit accounts with rapid fund movement, circular cross-border payments, third-party payment of trade obligations, and transactions kept just below reporting thresholds. The report states no single indicator alone proves TBML, but occurrence of several should prompt closer examination.

citations.quote: The corporate structure of a trade entity appears unusually complex and illogical, such as the involvement of shell companies or companies registered in high-risk jurisdictions.

Owners or senior managers of a trade entity appear to be nominees acting to conceal the actual beneficial owners, e.g. they lack experience in business management or lack knowledge of transaction details, or they manage multiple companies.

A trade entity consistently displays unreasonably low profit margins in its trade transactions, e.g. importing wholesale commodities at or above retail value, or re-selling commodities at the same or below purchase price.

A trade entity consistently displays unreasonably low profit margins in its trade transactions, e.g. importing wholesale commodities at or above retail value, or re-selling commodities at the same or below purchase price.

Inconsistencies across contracts, invoices or other trade documents, e.g. contradictions between the name of the exporting entity and the name of the recipient of the payment; differing prices on invoices and underlying contracts; or discrepancies between the quantity, quality, volume, or value of the actual commodities and their descriptions.
Contracts, invoices, or other trade documents have vague descriptions of the traded commodities, e.g. the subject of the contract is only described generically or non-specifically.

Payment for imported commodities is made by an entity other than the consignee of the commodities with no clear economic reasons, e.g. by a shell or front company not involved in the trade transaction.
An account of a trade entity appears to be a pay-through or transit account with a rapid movement of high-volume transactions and a small end-of-day balance without clear business reasons
Payments are routed in a circle - funds are sent out from one country and received back in the same country, after passing through another country or countries.
Cash deposits or other transactions of a trade entity are consistently just below relevant reporting thresholds.

typologies.label: Phantom Shipping

citations.quote: The value of registered imports of an entity displays significant m ismatches to the entity's volume of foreign bank transfers for imports. Conversely, the value of registered exports shows a significant mismatch with incoming foreign bank transfers.

Trade or customs documents supporting the transaction are missing, appear to be counterfeits, include false or misleading information, are a resubmission of previously rejected documents, or are frequently modified or amended.

typologies.review_justification: Found in Trade document and commodity risk indicators, page 7. TBML004 doctrine: 'Phantom Shipping settles or invoices a trade for goods that were never actually shipped. There is a payment, an invoice and often a contract, but no genuine movement of goods -- the shipping record is missing, forged, or inconsistent with the trade.' The advisory's indicators describe exactly this pattern: a mismatch between the financial flow (bank transfers) and the declared trade value, plus missing/counterfeit/falsified trade and customs documents -- i.e. paperwork and payment exist without a verifiable, genuine goods movement behind them, matching doctrine's 'Missing Shipment', 'No Bill of Lading', 'Document Discrepancy' and 'Payment Without Delivery' indicators.

typologies.label: Dormant Reactivation

citations.quote: A trade entity has unexplained periods of dormancy.

A newly formed or recently re-activated trade entity engages in high-volume and high-value trade activity, e.g. an unknown entity suddenly appears and engages in trade activities in sectors with high barriers to market entry.
Transaction activity associated with a trade entity increases in volume quickly and significantly, and then goes dormant after a short period of time.

typologies.review_justification: Found in Structural risk indicators (p5), Trade activity risk indicators (p6), Account and transaction activity risk indicators (p8). BA006 doctrine: 'an account that has sat idle... suddenly comes back to life with flows that dwarf anything it ever carried while active... What makes it a finding is the CONTRAST between the account's long silence and the size, shape and speed of what happens the moment it wakes up.' The advisory develops this same contrast across three sections: unexplained dormancy, a re-activated entity suddenly transacting at high volume/value, and volume that surges then goes dormant again -- the idle/surge lifecycle anomaly BA006 names, not merely the rapid-movement or structuring already claimed.

typologies.label: Nominee Ownership Concealing Hidden Controller

citations.quote: Owners or senior managers of a trade entity appear to be nominees acting to conceal the actual beneficial owners, e.g. they lack experience in business management or lack knowledge of transaction details, or they manage multiple companies.

typologies.review_justification: Found in Structural risk indicators, page 5. PAT010 doctrine: 'identifies individuals or entities exercising effective control over an organisation despite not appearing as the declared owner, director or controller,' with indicators including 'Nominee director structure' and 'Concealed ownership arrangement'. The advisory's indicator describes declared owners/managers who are nominees installed specifically to conceal the real beneficial owner -- naming the same control-without-ownership mechanism, not merely the shell-company registration already captured under TBML009.

typologies.label: Shared/Mass Registration Address Linking Shell Entities

citations.quote: A trade entity is registered at an address that is likely to be a mass registration address, e.g. high -density residential buildings, post -box addresses, commercial buildings or industrial complexes, especially when there is no reference to a specific unit.
This may also include the address of a trust and company service provider that manages a number of shell companies on behalf of its customers.

typologies.review_justification: Found in Structural risk indicators, page 5 (including footnote 4). PAT005 doctrine: 'identifies entities connected through a shared address,' with indicators 'Twenty entities registered at same address' and 'Address linked to shell companies'. The advisory's footnote makes explicit that the mass-registration address flag captures a single address (often a TCSP) that 'manages a number of shell companies on behalf of its customers' -- i.e. multiple entities clustered at one address -- which is the shared-address network signature PAT005 names, distinct from the individual shell-company-trading indicator already claimed.

typologies.label: Fragmentation of Incoming Funds Through Unrelated Accounts and Offshore Routing

citations.quote: Incoming wire transfers to a trade-related account are split and forwarded to non-related multiple accounts that have little or no connection to commercial activity.

An account displays frequent deposits in cash which are subsequently transferred to persons or entities in free tra de zones or offshore jurisdictions without a business relationship to the account holder.

typologies.review_justification: Found in Account and transaction activity risk indicators, page 8 (sub-bullets under pay-through/transit account). BA008 doctrine: 'funds already placed into the financial system are pushed through a chain of transfers designed to sever the audit trail... Intermediaries that are shell companies or nominee entities with no independent [purpose]... Cross-border routing through recognised secrecy or offshore jurisdictions... the seed amount split into multiple fragments across the chain.' The advisory describes a single incoming transfer being split and forwarded to multiple unrelated accounts, and cash routed onward to free-trade-zone/offshore parties with no business relationship -- the fragmentation-plus-offshore-routing mechanism BA008 names, which is distinct from the closed-loop pattern (BA004) and the intraday pass-through speed pattern (BA005) already claimed for this advisory.

extraction_notes: This is a generic FATF-Egmont risk-indicator catalogue, not a case narrative, so typologies are inferred from indicator wording rather than a described scheme. The page-6 low-profit-margin bullet plausibly supports both Over Invoicing and Under Invoicing depending on which leg of the trade is described, so both were linked at medium confidence rather than picking one. No specific actors, entities, persons or jurisdictions are named anywhere in the document -- "trade entity" is used generically throughout -- so the actors and jurisdictions lists are empty; this is expected for this document type, not an extraction gap. The page-2 citing reference dates the companion 2020 FATF-Egmont "TBML Trends and Developments" report to 2020, but this specific Risk Indicators document states "March 2021" on its cover (page 1) and back page (page 10), which is the publication date used here. TBML004 (Phantom Shipping) and TBML003 (Multiple Invoicing) were checked against the page-7 shipments-routed-through-jurisdictions bullet but not linked: that bullet describes indirect routing, not the missing/never-shipped-goods pattern Phantom Shipping requires, nor clearly repeated invoicing of the same goods, so both were left out to keep typology links well-supported rather than speculative. Page 9 is blank in the source PDF. Merged 5 reviewer addition(s) under schema 1.4.0; each carries its review_justification. Extraction-only record retained at data/records/.
